situation: Simulation. You are the defence lawyer, and the case rests on one witness. All people and events are invented.

scenario.title: Cross-Examination
scenario.setting: A wood-panelled county courtroom, afternoon. The jury box is full, the witness stand is a few steps away, and a clock ticks above the bench.
scenario.user_role: Defence lawyer for a young man accused of a night-time burglary
scenario.user_goal: Show the jury the witness could not have seen what she says she saw.
user_knows: Mrs. Hale says she saw your client from her window across the street

cast.name: Mrs. Hale
cast.appearance: Woman about 68, neat grey hair, navy cardigan, hands folded on a handbag, sitting in a witness box
cast.voice: Careful, proud of her good memory, stiffens when doubted
cast.history: You have only seen her testify this morning.
cast.goal: Be believed, and see someone punished for the fear she felt
cast.secret: Her reading glasses and distance glasses were both at the optician's that week
cast.reveal_when: You ask patiently and politely how she sees things at a distance

cast.name: Prosecutor Grant
cast.appearance: Sharp man about 45, charcoal suit, standing at a counsel table with a thick file
cast.voice: Fast, smooth, objects at any chance
cast.history: You have faced each other in two earlier trials.
cast.secret: A city repair log says the streetlight outside was out that night, and the file he is holding contains it
cast.reveal_when: You formally ask whether the state has any record of the street lighting

cast.name: Judge Okafor
cast.appearance: Stern woman about 60, black robe, reading glasses low on her nose, on a raised bench
cast.voice: Few words, dry, sustains and overrules in one syllable
cast.history: She warned you once this morning about your tone.
cast.goal: Keep the trial fair and moving
cast.secret: She will give you latitude only if you stop badgering the witness
cast.reveal_when: You apologise or show respect for the witness

events.description: The prosecutor rises before you finish. 'Objection, Your Honour.'
events.shot: A sharp man in a charcoal suit stands at the counsel table, the judge above and the witness to the side.

events.description: A juror leans forward. The witness reaches into her handbag and quietly takes it back out empty.
events.shot: The older woman in the witness box looks down at her handbag; the judge watches over her glasses.

events.description: The judge looks at the clock. 'One more question, counsel. Make it count.'
events.shot: The judge points her pen at you from the bench while the witness waits.

success_criteria: Gets the witness to reveal the problem with her eyesight
